Two BOM artifacts introduced by the mutation round-trips (a BOM added to RemoteActorRegistry.cs and NetClientLocalCombatDriver.cs, and one stripped from NetServerActor.cs) were detected via git diff and corrected before commit.

beforeAfter.before: A networked client: local body believes team 0 whatever the server says (Player Fps Actor.prefab:757 team: 0, latched by FpsActorController.Awake:159 into a static that never moves again); ScoreUi.UpdateUi repaints both score labels from a locally-counted MatchScoreboard on every capture flip, and SetAuthoritativeState's unchanged-input early-return means the server's numbers are not restored until they themselves change; RemoteActorRegistry marks every live remote actor, so every enemy inside InterestManager.CullRadius is on the minimap; ServerPlayerSlotPool.Fill creates Config.MaxConnections AI-driven bodies that are invisible to clients (X-18 holds them out of the announce and the snapshot) yet still shoot and score — 14 surplus at 16 slots with 2 humans, on top of the authored 20/20.
beforeAfter.after: The local body takes ActorSnapshotEntry.Team through ILocalPlayerRig.SetTeam — the same Actor.SetTeam the offline path uses, so the two skinned renderers are recoloured — applied by a poll that lands on whichever of body-or-snapshot arrives second, and written once. playerTeam is a property over the body, so the latch class is gone. The three engine-side offline mutators are gated on NetContext.IsOffline and ScoreUi does not subscribe Changed on a networked client. The minimap marks a body only when its team equals the resolved local team, in both directions and at spawn as well as per-frame. A player-slot body is created with its bot brain parked, and the server logs the parked count. Five detectors, each observed red first: G15 in ClientWiringGate (two independent call sites), and three EditMode fixtures covering D-1, D-3 and D-4.
